Task Guide: Task: Compute the bulk modulus of Aluminum by applying small finite deformations and calculating the full elastic constant tensor, followed by the Voigt averaging method. Simulate a face centered cubic lattice structure for Aluminum using LAMMPS with a lattice constant of 4.05 angstrom. The simulation should use metal units, define a 5x5x5 simulation box, and set periodic boundary conditions to True in all directions. Use the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Aluminum. First, relax the simulation box to zero pressure using the box/relax fix and perform energy minimization with a force tolerance of 1e-10, energy tolerance of 0.0, maximum iterations of 100, and maximum evaluations of 1000. Save the relaxed structure. Then, apply small symmetric deformations in each of the six independent strain directions, and after each deformation, perform energy minimization to relax the atomic positions using the same minimization parameters. From the stress response of each deformation, compute the full elastic constant tensor, and calculate the bulk modulus using the Voigt average formula. Report the final value of the bulk modulus in GPa. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/gpt_4o/brief/task_5/task_5_trial_4 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL.
